invariantRules.text: Control identity survives revision, owner change, implementation change, re-estimation, register movement, split, merge, closure and assessment turnover.
Changing objective, mechanism, applicability, cadence or dependency creates an immutable successor definition revision under the same control identity.
Owner authority is identity-level; owner change appends an authority state and never mutates a definition revision.
An effective control cites exactly one approved effective definition revision; new reliance cannot cite withdrawn, retired or superseded revisions.
Control existence, documentation, implementation or policy status never proves effectiveness or closes risk.
Design adequacy, implementation state, operating state, execution occurrence and effectiveness conclusion are distinct assertions.
Implementation and operating states are time-bounded identity-owned records and never mutate an immutable definition revision.
Execution occurrences and telemetry remain external evidence and never become control revisions or states.
One control cited by many risks never merges risk identities or assessments.
Control identity supersession and definition-revision supersession are distinct; both preserve historical resolution and mark affected contexts stale.
Superseded identity requires successor reference; retired identity requires retired time; superseded revision requires effective end and successor revision.
Control and revision identifiers remain immutable, resolvable and never recycled.
Operation is one of operating, suspended or not-operating and records expected versus observed occurrences by external reference.
